text:
Exponential weighting of later window losses is not a clean test of preference recency. For a zero-initialized GRU, later nonpadding positions also have more recurrent context; window-relative position need not indicate proximity to the end of the user’s complete training history. Analytical implication: target t receives expected weight Σw P(w)·1[t∈w]·a(position(t,w)), so overlapping-window inclusion and boundary effects further alter target exposure. Left-padding indices can additionally confound position with sequence length; measure context using actual preceding items.

Closest literature: [Tan et al. (2016)](https://arxiv.org/html/1606.08117) train GRUs on every prefix with terminal next-item supervision and fixed-length BPTT; separately examine temporal adaptation using recent-data fine-tuning. These distinguish sequence preprocessing from calendar recency, but do not fully disentangle the proposed weighting. [Petrov and Macdonald’s RSS](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643) explicitly samples targets using exponential position-based importance, compares against sequence continuation on GRU4Rec, and varies recency strength. However, RSS removes sampled targets and changes the prediction task: its gains do not establish that exponentially weighting causal window losses captures preference drift. Neither study provides the exact three-factor control requested.

Affordable proposed control: retain identical sampled windows, negatives, initialization and updates, but replace positional weights with each window’s mean valid-position weight. This preserves total window emphasis while removing preference for longer recurrent contexts within a window. For stronger separation, sample training targets uniformly and give each exactly K preceding items; compare uniform losses against exponential weights based on distance from the full training-history end, correcting unequal target inclusion probabilities if necessary. This fixes context length while varying recency. Fit each condition independently, without fusion; select using the pinned macro validation HR@10.
